claims.text: The component alloy is susceptible to hot cracking during traditional fusion-welding repair.
Traditional fusion-welding repair causes deleterious microstructural changes and compromised mechanical performance in this material.
Friction stir processing can repair the damaged region without melting the material.
A rotating FSP tool generates severe plastic deformation and localized sub-melting heat.
FSP-induced deformation and controlled heating promote dynamic recrystallization.
FSP-induced deformation and controlled heating homogenize the repair-zone microstructure.
FSP produces a finely recrystallized and grain-refined microstructure in the repair zone.
FSP reduces residual stresses in the processed repair zone.
Keeping the material below a fully molten state prevents the hot-crack formation typical of fusion welding.
The FSP repair zone will be free from hot cracks.
The refined FSP microstructure will restore mechanical integrity.
An FSP-repaired region will have greater toughness than a traditionally fusion-welded repair.
An FSP-repaired region will have greater fatigue resistance than a traditionally fusion-welded repair.
Under aggressive operating conditions, the FSP-repaired region will retain integrity and service life closer to the original material than a fusion-welded repair.
Tool rotation and traverse speeds must be selected to keep the peak processing temperature below the alloy melting point.
